sources.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons July 2026 download
verified_facts: The current INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset was published on 5 July 2026.
New files are published on the first Sunday of every month.
Files are downloadable by local authority under Open Government Licence conditions.
semantic_limits: Publication freshness does not prove that a particular polygon changed in the current month.
INSPIRE polygons show indicative extent and position and are not exact legal boundary determinations.

sources.name: INSPIRE GML technical guidance
verified_facts: HM Land Registry polygon data is captured against British National Grid.
EPSG:27700 is the native projection used for the polygon workflow.
Reprojection from British National Grid to WGS84 can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
semantic_limits: WGS84 coordinates remain display-only for this measurement workflow.
Exact point-in-polygon and raster sampling must remain in native EPSG:27700.

sources.name: LIDAR Composite DTM 1m metadata
verified_facts: The coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The published vertical accuracy is plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
semantic_limits: Dataset-level RMSE is an uncertainty input, not a parcel-specific guarantee.
A parcel result still requires exact HMLR polygon binding, valid pixel masking and hash-backed source bytes.

sources.name: OS Terrain 5 product supply
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is supplied as 5 metre grid or contour data in 5 kilometre by 5 kilometre tiles.
The product is resupplied quarterly in January, April, July and October.
The full national grid supply is distributed as compressed tiles.
semantic_limits: OS Terrain 5 remains a secondary sanity check and cannot replace EA DTM 1m for sub-metre parcel measurement.
A product update schedule does not prove that a specific tile changed.

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 documentation and accuracy
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
Grid data uses regular 50 metre post spacing and 10 kilometre by 10 kilometre tiles.
The official overview reports 4 metre RMSE for the grid data.
semantic_limits: OS Terrain 50 is only a broad secondary crosscheck.
Its 50 metre resolution and 4 metre RMSE cannot validate sub-metre parcel height differences by itself.
